title: Corporate web proxy no Kerberos authentication for iframe content since Firefox 108.0.1
body: Since Firefox updated to 108.0.1, pages behind our corporate proxy load normally except for embedded iframe content. Firefox sends Kerberos authentication for the rest of the page but not for the iframe requests, so the proxy refuses those connections. We see the missing authentication in the proxy logs. This happens on different laptops and virtual machines, including Beta and Nightly. Older Firefox versions work, and there was no change to our corporate proxy.

symptoms_visible: Since Firefox 108.0.1, the main page loads through our Kerberos-authenticated corporate proxy, but embedded iframe content is refused because Firefox sends no authentication for those requests.
I see the same behavior on different laptops and virtual machines; older Firefox versions load the iframe content correctly.
N0.label: N0 iframe proxy authentication regression reported

symptoms_visible: The main page still loads, while iframe requests through the corporate proxy are refused without Kerberos authentication.
N1.label: N1 mozregression output collected

symptoms_visible: Iframe content remains unavailable through the proxy while the rest of the page loads.
N2.label: N2 HTTP log supplied privately

symptoms_visible: I found no option to disable X-Frame-Options, and our proxy does not manipulate website content; the iframe still receives the proxy refusal instead of loading.
N2_x.label: N2_x proxy X-Frame-Options workaround rejected

symptoms_visible: Does this mean I can already test whether the problem is gone in the latest Nightly build? I haven't retested the affected page yet.
N3.label: N3 backout build installed, unverified

symptoms_visible: In today's Nightly the page loads completely again — the embedded iframe content comes through the corporate proxy without the refusal error.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you run mozregression to determine which Firefox change introduced the iframe authentication problem?
Please bisect between an older working Firefox build and the affected version and share the final mozregression output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran mozregression. It ended on the 2022-11-11 Firefox 108.0a1 Nightly build, changeset b7164776589657b7d7fd40d32268b2a489eed789. The pushlog is https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/pushloghtml?fromchange=df541ee6f62267803ead2b4e966dc2c06a23c58a&tochange=b7164776589657b7d7fd40d32268b2a489eed789.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Mozregression shows the iframe requests already failed in every older build I tested, with no Firefox regression window.
I got the same pushlog range while starting from a different known-good older Firefox build.

edges.comment: The reporter supplied the raw mozregression build metadata, changeset, and pushlog. Mapping this range to bug 1629307 was performed later by engineers.

question_patterns: Can you record an HTTP log while reproducing the failed iframe request and send it privately because it may contain sensitive information?
Please capture Firefox networking logs for one affected page load and email the file to the networking engineer.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I recorded the HTTP log and sent the file to you by email.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce the failure while logging; the iframe authenticates and loads normally in every logged run.
I sent the same log as a compressed archive instead of an uncompressed file.

edges.comment: The HTTP log was sent privately and is not an available attachment. The reporter only confirmed sending it; the X-Frame-Options lines and their interpretation came from the engineer's inspection.

question_patterns: Could you confirm whether the X-Frame-Options header is added by your proxy or by the original site?
Is the XFO: deny coming from the proxy response or from the origin server?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I guess the X-Frame-Options: deny you are seeing in the logs is the answer from the corporate proxy — because no authentication was sent for Kerberos, the proxy answers with an NTLM negotiate as a fallback. I found no option to disable any X-Frame-Options; we do not manipulate any content of the website with the proxy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The header is definitely set by the origin site itself; the proxy passes responses through untouched.

solution.intent: Treat X-Frame-Options: deny as a proxy-added policy and temporarily disable that header on the corporate proxy.
solution.concrete_example: The HTTP log contains X-Frame-Options: deny. Confirm whether the proxy adds it and, if so, disable that header temporarily so the iframe can load.
solution.inference_hint: The engineer, not the reporter, extracted the X-Frame-Options: deny line from the private HTTP log. The proposed proxy-header workaround was rejected because the reporter found no such option and explained that the proxy does not rewrite site content; the header was part of the unauthenticated proxy response.

edges.comment: Real thread c9-c11: the engineer proposed disabling a supposedly proxy-added X-Frame-Options header. The reporter could not do so and explained that the proxy only scans for malicious content; this direction did not resolve the issue. [Round-5: c10 was a mixed turn — the header-origin question plus the conditional disable suggestion; re-typed accordingly.]

solution.intent: Back out the bug 1629307 iframe X-Frame-Options authentication suppression and use a Firefox build containing that backout, restoring proxy authentication for embedded content.
solution.concrete_example: Use a Firefox build containing the backout of bug 1629307, such as the verified Nightly or Firefox 109.0.1 and later fixed builds. The backout restores the authentication path for iframe requests whose unauthenticated proxy response carries X-Frame-Options: deny.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers mapped the reporter's raw mozregression range to bug 1629307 and read the private HTTP log. That change avoided authentication prompts for iframe responses that appeared destined to fail an X-Frame-Options/CSP check. Here, the X-Frame-Options: deny response came from the unauthenticated proxy exchange, so applying the check before completing proxy authentication prevented the Kerberos-authenticated iframe request. The reporter did not independently derive this mechanism.

edges.comment: Reshaped per round-3 audit to the fix-then-verify pattern: identify bug 1629307 as the regressor and back it out / move the user to a build containing the backout. Proposed on the pre-fix evidence (mozregression + HTTP log reading).

question_patterns: Please retest the affected page in today's Nightly build and tell me what you see.
Can you install the current Nightly and report whether the iframe content loads through the proxy?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can confirm, the issue is resolved in the nightly build from today. The page is now loading without any issues again!

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest Nightly still refuses the iframe request without Kerberos authentication.
The page and iframe both load correctly in the Nightly build after restarting Firefox once.

edges.comment: Verification after the backout landed (c23-c24); patterns are backout-agnostic so the retest request never names the fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: bug 1629307 suppressed authentication for iframe requests when an unauthenticated response appeared blocked by X-Frame-Options/CSP; the corporate proxy's unauthenticated response carried X-Frame-Options: deny, so Firefox failed to proceed with Kerberos proxy authentication.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the mozregression output and the privately supplied HTTP log, with the mapping to bug 1629307 and interpretation of the X-Frame-Options response treated as engineer inference.
Must recommend the backout of bug 1629307 or updating to a Firefox build containing that backout, rather than changing the corporate Kerberos deployment.

Must not present disabling X-Frame-Options on the corporate proxy as the fix; the reporter found no such option, the proxy did not rewrite website content, and that direction did not resolve the issue.
Must require successful reporter verification on a fixed build before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Enterprise IT administrator with practical knowledge of Kerberos-authenticated web proxies and access to proxy logs; able to run mozregression, capture HTTP logs, and test Nightly builds, but not a Firefox networking developer.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, concise, and cooperative; supplies requested diagnostics promptly, describes enterprise infrastructure behavior directly, and asks for confirmation before testing a newly landed build.
